entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Conrad Confalonieri of Piacenza, TOSF, was an Italian hermit of the Third Order of St. Francis, venerated as a saint.

Born in 1290s in Piacenza, Italy, Conrad Confalonieri dedicated his life to spiritual contemplation, exemplifying the ideals of the Franciscan Order. His solitary existence, though simple, had a profound impact on the devotional practices of his contemporaries.

Conrad's legacy extends beyond his individual piety; he played a significant role in shaping the devotional landscape of 14th-century Italy. His mystical writings, though largely unpublished during his lifetime, would later influence the development of Franciscan spirituality.

As a testament to his profound influence, Conrad's feast day, celebrated on February 27, solidifies his place within the canon of Italian saints, alongside figures like Saint Francis of Assisi.

The significance of Conrad's life lies not only in his personal devotion but also in the broader cultural and religious context of his time.

A notable example of the enduring power of Franciscan spirituality, Conrad's example continues to inspire contemporary Christians seeking a deeper connection with God.

Conrad Confalonieri's life, though marked by simplicity and solitude, holds a profound significance for those seeking to understand the evolution of Christian spirituality in the Middle Ages.
